A.5.1.o: Ensure security direction is set, approved by leadership, and communicated to everyone.
A.5.1.a: Write a set of information security policies, get management to formally approve them, publish them to staff, and review them on a fixed schedule.
A.5.1.e: The auditor checks that policies exist, were approved by management, reached staff, and are reviewed regularly.
A.5.1.r: Approved Information Security Policy; policy review log with dates; evidence staff received/acknowledged it.

A.5.2.o: Make sure every security responsibility has a clearly named owner.
A.5.2.a: Define who is responsible for each security task and record it in role descriptions and the tool's owner fields.
A.5.2.e: The auditor looks for defined, documented security roles with no gaps or overlaps.
A.5.2.r: Roles & responsibilities matrix; org chart; job descriptions with security duties.

A.5.3.o: Prevent fraud and error by splitting conflicting duties between different people.
A.5.3.a: Identify conflicting duties (e.g. request vs approve, develop vs deploy) and ensure no single person controls both.
A.5.3.e: The auditor tests whether one person can perform and approve a sensitive action alone.
A.5.3.r: Segregation-of-duties matrix; approval workflows; access reviews showing the split.

A.5.4.o: Ensure management actively requires staff to apply security, not just publish rules.
A.5.4.a: Have management set expectations, communicate them, and hold staff accountable for following policy.
A.5.4.e: The auditor looks for evidence management drives compliance, not just documents it.
A.5.4.r: Management communications; onboarding acknowledgements; policy sign-offs.

A.5.5.o: Be able to reach the right authorities quickly during an incident.
A.5.5.a: Maintain contact details for police, regulators and the data protection authority, and a short procedure for using them.
A.5.5.e: The auditor checks the contact list is current and staff know when to escalate.
A.5.5.r: Authority contact list; incident escalation procedure.

A.5.6.o: Stay informed through security communities and special interest groups.
A.5.6.a: Join relevant forums, mailing lists and industry groups, and use what you learn.
A.5.6.e: The auditor looks for active membership and evidence the intelligence is used.
A.5.6.r: Membership records; subscription lists; notes on advice acted upon.

A.5.7.o: Anticipate threats by collecting and acting on threat intelligence.
A.5.7.a: Subscribe to threat feeds/bulletins, review them, and feed findings into risk and controls.
A.5.7.e: The auditor checks threat information is collected and demonstrably acted on.
A.5.7.r: Threat intelligence feeds/reports; records of resulting actions or risk updates.

A.5.8.o: Build security into projects from the start rather than bolting it on later.
A.5.8.a: Add security requirements and reviews into your project method for every project.
A.5.8.e: The auditor samples projects for embedded security activities.
A.5.8.r: Project management template with security steps; security review records in projects.

A.5.9.o: Maintain an accurate inventory of information and assets, each with an owner.
A.5.9.a: Record all information assets with owner, type, classification and location, and keep it current.
A.5.9.e: The auditor checks the inventory is complete, owned and up to date.
A.5.9.r: The asset register (Assets); asset owner assignments.

A.5.10.o: Set and enforce acceptable rules for using information and assets.
A.5.10.a: Publish an Acceptable Use Policy and make staff accept it.
A.5.10.e: The auditor looks for defined usage rules and staff acceptance.
A.5.10.r: Acceptable Use Policy; signed staff acknowledgements.

A.5.11.o: Recover all assets when someone leaves or changes role.
A.5.11.a: Run an offboarding checklist that reclaims laptops, badges, tokens and access.
A.5.11.e: The auditor samples leavers to confirm assets were returned.
A.5.11.r: Completed offboarding checklists, attached as evidence; asset return records.

A.5.12.o: Classify information by sensitivity so it is handled correctly.
A.5.12.a: Define a classification scheme (e.g. Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) and apply it.
A.5.12.e: The auditor checks information is classified consistently against the scheme.
A.5.12.r: Classification scheme/policy; examples of classified assets (Asset Register).

A.5.13.o: Label information so its classification is obvious to handlers.
A.5.13.a: Apply labels to documents, emails and storage reflecting their classification.
A.5.13.e: The auditor samples information for correct labelling.

A.5.14.o: Protect information whenever it is transferred between people, systems or organisations.
A.5.14.a: Use secure channels (encryption, secure portals) and agreements for all information transfers.
A.5.14.e: The auditor reviews transfer mechanisms to confirm data cannot be intercepted or leaked in transit.
A.5.14.r: SFTP/secure transfer configs; TLS/encryption settings; signed data-transfer agreements.

A.5.15.o: Control who can access what, based on business need.
A.5.15.a: Define an access control policy and configure permissions to match it.
A.5.15.e: The auditor checks access is granted per policy and least privilege.
A.5.15.r: Access Control Policy; permission configurations; role definitions.

A.5.16.o: Manage every identity through its full life, uniquely tied to one person.
A.5.16.a: Create identities when needed, keep them unique (no shared accounts), and remove them when not.
A.5.16.e: The auditor tests joiner/leaver identity handling and looks for shared accounts.
A.5.16.r: Identity lifecycle procedure; joiner/leaver records; unique-account evidence.

A.5.17.o: Handle passwords and login secrets securely.
A.5.17.a: Set a password policy, use secure issuance/storage (password manager), and a safe reset process.
A.5.17.e: The auditor checks how secrets are issued, stored and reset.
A.5.17.r: Password/authentication policy; password manager usage; reset procedure.

A.5.18.o: Grant, review and revoke access rights formally.
A.5.18.a: Approve access requests, review access regularly, and remove access no longer needed.
A.5.18.e: The auditor samples access approvals and periodic access reviews.
A.5.18.r: Access request approvals; periodic access review reports (e.g. quarterly).

A.5.19.o: Manage security risks arising from supplier relationships.
A.5.19.a: Assess supplier security risk and track suppliers in the Suppliers register.
A.5.19.e: The auditor checks suppliers are risk-assessed and monitored.
A.5.19.r: Supplier security policy; the Suppliers register, with a risk level for each supplier.

A.5.20.o: Put security requirements into supplier agreements.
A.5.20.a: Include security and data-protection clauses in supplier contracts.
A.5.20.e: The auditor samples contracts for security clauses.
A.5.20.r: Contract security clauses; data processing agreements (DPAs).

A.5.21.o: Manage security risks across the ICT supply chain, not just direct suppliers.
A.5.21.a: Assess risks from sub-suppliers and components your services depend on.
A.5.21.e: The auditor checks supply-chain risk is considered beyond tier-1 suppliers.

A.5.22.o: Keep checking suppliers meet expectations and manage changes to their services.
A.5.22.a: Review suppliers on a schedule and control changes to the services they provide.
A.5.22.e: The auditor samples supplier reviews and change records.
A.5.22.r: Supplier review records with dates (Suppliers); service change logs.

A.5.23.o: Use cloud services securely, from selection to exit.
A.5.23.a: Set rules for choosing, configuring, using and leaving cloud services.
A.5.23.e: The auditor checks cloud usage is governed and securely configured.
A.5.23.r: Cloud usage policy; cloud security configuration/posture reports; exit plan.

A.5.24.o: Be ready to handle incidents before one happens.
A.5.24.a: Create an incident response plan defining roles, steps and communication.
A.5.24.e: The auditor looks for an approved, workable incident plan.
A.5.24.r: Approved Incident Response Plan; defined roles and contacts.

A.5.25.o: Assess events and decide which are security incidents.
A.5.25.a: Triage security events and record the decision on whether each is an incident.
A.5.25.e: The auditor samples events for consistent assessment decisions.
A.5.25.r: Event triage records; incident classification criteria.

A.5.26.o: Respond to incidents following defined procedures.
A.5.26.a: Work incidents through your documented response process and record actions.
A.5.26.e: The auditor reviews incident records for a proper, documented response.
A.5.26.r: Incident records with actions and outcomes (Incidents).

A.5.27.o: Learn from incidents so they don't recur.
A.5.27.a: Run post-incident reviews and raise corrective actions from lessons learned.
A.5.27.e: The auditor checks lessons are captured and drive improvement.
A.5.27.r: Post-incident review notes; the findings raised from them, with their corrective actions (Findings).

A.5.28.o: Preserve incident evidence properly in case it is needed legally.
A.5.28.a: Follow a procedure to collect and protect evidence about incidents.
A.5.28.e: The auditor checks evidence handling would stand up if challenged.

A.5.29.o: Keep security working during disruption or crisis.
A.5.29.a: Include security in business continuity plans and test them.
A.5.29.e: The auditor checks continuity plans address security and are tested.
A.5.29.r: Business continuity plan (security sections); BC test results.

A.5.30.o: Ensure IT can recover fast enough to meet business needs.
A.5.30.a: Maintain a disaster recovery plan and test recovery against targets.
A.5.30.e: The auditor checks recovery capability and test evidence.
A.5.30.r: Disaster recovery plan; recovery test records (RTO/RPO).

A.5.31.o: Know and meet every legal, regulatory and contractual security requirement.
A.5.31.a: Maintain a register of applicable requirements and keep it current.
A.5.31.e: The auditor checks legal/contractual obligations are identified and met.

A.5.32.a: Use only properly licensed software and content; track licences.
A.5.32.e: The auditor checks for licence compliance and unlicensed software.
A.5.32.r: Software licence inventory; software audit results.

A.5.33.o: Protect important records from loss, tampering and unauthorised access.
A.5.33.a: Set retention rules and protect key records with access control and backups.
A.5.33.e: The auditor checks records are retained and protected appropriately.
A.5.33.r: Records retention schedule; protected storage evidence; backups.

A.5.34.o: Protect personal data in line with privacy law.
A.5.34.a: Maintain a privacy policy, data inventory and processing agreements.
A.5.34.e: The auditor checks personal data is handled lawfully and protected.
A.5.34.r: Privacy policy; data inventory / RoPA; DPAs.

A.5.35.o: Have security reviewed independently at planned intervals.
A.5.35.a: Arrange internal or external independent reviews of your security.
A.5.35.e: The auditor looks for independent review evidence.
A.5.35.r: Internal audit reports (Audits & reviews); independent review records.

A.5.36.o: Check that people and systems actually follow policies and standards.
A.5.36.a: Verify compliance through reviews, manager checks and the tool's status tracking.
A.5.36.e: The auditor samples for evidence of active compliance checking.
A.5.36.r: Compliance check records; management reviews; control status tracking.

A.5.37.o: Document operating procedures so key tasks are done correctly every time.
A.5.37.a: Write runbooks/procedures for important tasks and make them available.
A.5.37.e: The auditor checks documented procedures exist and are used.

A.6.1.o: Check people's backgrounds before hiring, proportionate to risk.
A.6.1.a: Run screening/reference checks appropriate to each role before granting access.
A.6.1.e: The auditor samples new hires for screening evidence.

A.6.2.o: Put security responsibilities into employment terms.
A.6.2.a: Include security obligations in employment contracts.
A.6.2.e: The auditor samples contracts for security terms.
A.6.2.r: Employment contract security clauses; signed agreements.

A.6.3.o: Keep everyone aware and trained in security, relevant to their role.
A.6.3.a: Deliver regular awareness training and record who completed it.
A.6.3.e: The auditor checks training happened and coverage is high.

A.6.4.o: Have a fair, formal process for security rule breaches.
A.6.4.a: Define a disciplinary process for security violations and make staff aware.
A.6.4.e: The auditor checks a documented disciplinary process exists.

A.6.5.o: Enforce security duties that continue after employment ends or changes.
A.6.5.a: Define surviving obligations and complete offboarding for every leaver/mover.
A.6.5.e: The auditor samples leavers to confirm duties and access were handled.
A.6.5.r: Post-employment clauses; offboarding records, attached as evidence.

A.6.6.o: Protect shared information with confidentiality agreements.
A.6.6.a: Use NDAs with staff and third parties and keep them on file.
A.6.6.e: The auditor samples for signed NDAs where required.

A.6.7.a: Set a remote working policy and enforce VPN and device security.
A.6.7.e: The auditor checks remote-work controls are defined and applied.
A.6.7.r: Remote working policy; VPN and device security settings.

A.6.8.o: Give staff an easy way to report security events.
A.6.8.a: Provide a reporting channel, make staff aware of it, and act on reports.
A.6.8.e: The auditor checks the channel exists, is known, and is used.
A.6.8.r: Reporting channel/procedure; awareness evidence; reports received.

A.7.1.o: Define secure physical perimeters around sensitive areas.
A.7.1.a: Establish physical boundaries and barriers around areas holding sensitive systems/info.
A.7.1.e: The auditor inspects perimeters and boundary controls.
A.7.1.r: Site/floor plan showing secure areas; physical barrier evidence.

A.7.2.o: Control who physically enters secure areas.
A.7.2.a: Use badge/entry controls and visitor logs for secure areas.
A.7.2.e: The auditor reviews entry records and access to secure areas.
A.7.2.r: Access control system records; visitor logs.

A.7.3.o: Physically secure offices, rooms and facilities.
A.7.3.a: Lock and restrict access to sensitive rooms and facilities.
A.7.3.e: The auditor inspects physical security of key rooms.
A.7.3.r: Physical security measures; access restriction evidence.

A.7.4.o: Monitor premises for unauthorised physical access.
A.7.4.a: Use CCTV, alarms and monitoring for sensitive locations.
A.7.4.e: The auditor checks monitoring is in place and reviewed.

A.7.5.o: Protect against physical and environmental threats.
A.7.5.a: Put in place fire, flood and power protections and monitoring.
A.7.5.e: The auditor checks environmental protections and tests.
A.7.5.r: Fire suppression; environmental sensors; maintenance/test records.

A.7.6.o: Set rules for working inside secure areas.
A.7.6.a: Define and enforce secure-area working procedures.
A.7.6.e: The auditor checks secure-area rules exist and are followed.

A.7.7.o: Keep desks clear and screens locked when unattended.
A.7.7.a: Enforce a clear desk / clear screen policy with spot checks.
A.7.7.e: The auditor may inspect the workplace and check policy.
A.7.7.r: Clear desk/clear screen policy; spot-check results; screen-lock settings.

A.7.8.o: Site and protect equipment against damage and prying eyes.
A.7.8.a: Position equipment to reduce risk of damage and unauthorised viewing.
A.7.8.r: Equipment siting standards; server room/screen positioning evidence.

A.7.9.a: Secure laptops and devices taken outside the premises (encryption, rules).
A.7.9.e: The auditor checks off-site asset protection.
A.7.9.r: Off-site asset policy; device encryption reports.

A.7.10.o: Manage storage media securely through its whole life.
A.7.10.a: Control media handling and securely dispose of or wipe media.
A.7.10.e: The auditor checks media handling and disposal.
A.7.10.r: Media handling policy; secure disposal/wipe records.

A.7.11.e: The auditor checks supporting utilities and tests.
A.7.11.r: UPS/generator inventory; maintenance and test records.

A.7.12.o: Protect cabling from interference and damage.
A.7.12.a: Follow cabling standards and protect power/network runs.
A.7.12.r: Cabling standards; protected cable run evidence.

A.7.13.o: Maintain equipment to keep it available and secure.
A.7.13.a: Follow maintenance schedules and log the work.
A.7.13.e: The auditor checks maintenance is performed and recorded.

A.7.14.o: Wipe or destroy data before disposing of or reusing equipment.
A.7.14.a: Securely erase or destroy media before disposal or reuse.

A.8.1.o: Secure every endpoint that touches company information.
A.8.1.a: Manage and secure laptops, desktops and phones (encryption, MDM).
A.8.1.e: The auditor checks endpoint protection coverage.
A.8.1.r: MDM/endpoint policy; disk encryption reports; device inventory.

A.8.2.a: Limit, approve and regularly review privileged accounts.
A.8.2.e: The auditor samples privileged accounts and their approvals/reviews.
A.8.2.r: Privileged account list; approvals; periodic privileged access reviews.

A.8.3.o: Restrict information access to those who need it.
A.8.3.a: Configure access so users only reach what their role requires.
A.8.3.e: The auditor tests access against need-to-know.

A.8.4.o: Control access to source code and dev tools.
A.8.4.a: Restrict who can read/change source code and protect branches.
A.8.4.e: The auditor checks repository access and controls.

A.8.5.o: Use strong authentication, including MFA where it matters.
A.8.5.a: Enforce strong sign-in and multi-factor authentication on key systems.
A.8.5.e: The auditor checks MFA and authentication strength.

A.8.6.o: Manage capacity so systems keep running.
A.8.6.a: Monitor storage/compute/people capacity and plan ahead.
A.8.6.e: The auditor checks capacity is monitored and planned.

A.8.7.o: Protect against malware with tools and awareness.
A.8.7.a: Deploy anti-malware/EDR and train users to spot threats.
A.8.7.e: The auditor checks malware protection coverage and awareness.
A.8.7.r: Antivirus/EDR coverage reports; malware awareness training records.

A.8.8.o: Find and fix technical vulnerabilities in good time.
A.8.8.a: Scan for vulnerabilities and patch within defined timeframes.
A.8.8.e: The auditor checks scanning cadence and remediation SLAs.
A.8.8.r: Vulnerability scan reports; patch records; remediation SLA/policy.

A.8.9.o: Configure systems securely and keep them that way.
A.8.9.a: Apply hardened baselines and monitor for configuration drift.
A.8.9.e: The auditor checks secure baselines and drift monitoring.
A.8.9.r: Configuration baselines/standards; config monitoring or posture reports.

A.8.10.o: Delete information when no longer needed.
A.8.10.a: Apply deletion rules and record deletions.
A.8.10.e: The auditor checks data is deleted per rules.

A.8.11.o: Mask sensitive data where full detail is not required.
A.8.11.a: Mask or anonymise data in test and non-essential contexts.
A.8.11.e: The auditor checks masking where appropriate.
A.8.11.r: Data masking settings; anonymised test data samples.

A.8.12.a: Deploy data leakage prevention on email, uploads and devices.
A.8.12.e: The auditor checks DLP rules and alerts.

A.8.13.o: Back up information and prove restores work.
A.8.13.a: Back up systems/data and test restores regularly.
A.8.13.e: The auditor checks backups run and restores are tested.
A.8.13.r: Backup configuration; successful restore test records.

A.8.14.o: Build in redundancy so single failures don't take you down.
A.8.14.a: Provide redundant infrastructure and test failover.
A.8.14.e: The auditor checks redundancy and failover tests.

A.8.15.o: Record, protect and review activity logs.
A.8.15.a: Enable logging, protect logs, and review them.
A.8.15.e: The auditor checks logging coverage, retention and review.
A.8.15.r: Logging configuration; log retention settings; log review notes.

A.8.16.a: Monitor and alert on anomalies that could indicate attacks.
A.8.16.e: The auditor checks monitoring and investigated alerts.

A.8.17.o: Keep clocks synchronised so logs line up.

A.8.18.o: Restrict powerful utilities that can bypass controls.
A.8.18.a: Limit and control use of privileged utility programs.
A.8.18.e: The auditor checks utility use is restricted and logged.

A.8.19.o: Control software installation on operational systems.
A.8.19.a: Govern what software can be installed via allow-listing and change control.
A.8.19.e: The auditor checks installation is controlled.
A.8.19.r: Software installation policy; allow-list; change approvals.

A.8.20.a: Configure and manage network security to protect data in transit.
A.8.20.e: The auditor reviews network security configuration.

A.8.21.o: Secure network services and hold providers to requirements.
A.8.21.a: Define security requirements for network services and enforce them.
A.8.21.e: The auditor checks service security requirements and delivery.

A.8.22.o: Segregate networks so a breach can't reach everything.
A.8.22.a: Split networks into zones (VLANs/segments) to contain breaches.
A.8.22.r: Network diagram showing segmentation; VLAN/segment configuration.

A.8.23.o: Filter access to dangerous or inappropriate sites.
A.8.23.e: The auditor checks web filtering is in place.

A.8.24.o: Use cryptography properly, including key management.
A.8.24.a: Apply encryption to the right data and manage keys securely.
A.8.24.e: The auditor checks encryption use and key management.
A.8.24.r: Cryptography policy; encryption standards; key management records.

A.8.25.o: Build security into the whole development lifecycle.
A.8.25.a: Define a secure development lifecycle with security gates.
A.8.25.e: The auditor checks security is built into development.
A.8.25.r: Secure development policy; pipeline security gate evidence.

A.8.26.o: Define the security an application must have.
A.8.26.a: Set security requirements for apps you build or buy.
A.8.26.e: The auditor checks security requirements exist and are met.
A.8.26.r: Application security requirements in specs/purchase decisions.

A.8.27.o: Design systems using secure architecture principles.
A.8.27.a: Apply secure architecture and engineering principles in design.
A.8.27.e: The auditor reviews design and architecture decisions.

A.8.28.o: Write code securely so common flaws never appear.
A.8.28.a: Follow secure coding standards and use code analysis tools.
A.8.28.e: The auditor checks coding standards and analysis results.
A.8.28.r: Secure coding standards; SAST/code analysis reports.

A.8.29.o: Test security during development and before go-live.
A.8.29.a: Run security testing in development and at acceptance.
A.8.29.e: The auditor checks security testing evidence.
A.8.29.r: Security test reports; penetration test results.

A.8.30.o: Keep control of security when development is outsourced.
A.8.30.a: Set security requirements for outsourced development and review the output.
A.8.30.e: The auditor checks outsourced work meets security requirements.

A.8.31.a: Keep environments separate with different access and credentials.

A.8.32.a: Manage changes through a defined process with approvals and rollback.
A.8.32.e: The auditor samples changes for proper control.
A.8.32.r: Change management policy; change requests/approvals; rollback plans.

A.8.33.a: Avoid real data in testing; protect any test data used.
A.8.33.e: The auditor checks test data handling.
A.8.33.r: Test data policy; anonymised test datasets.

A.8.34.o: Protect live systems during audits and tests.
A.8.34.a: Agree scope and protections before audit tests touch production.
A.8.34.e: The auditor checks audit activities were controlled.
A.8.34.r: Agreed audit scope/access; protective arrangements during testing.
